title: Latency Gatekeeper Runbook: calendar + smoke checklist + release notes (apr-2027 wip)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for a small-surface release that introduces routing and batching changes intended to reduce tail token latency on hosted API. The idea: use a latency gatekeeper stage in the rollout that actively compares p50/p95/p99 and KV-cache hit rate against baseline and holds traffic if thresholds exceed tolerances.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies only to hosted-api routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat (customer tier: standard).
- We will roll to 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with a 30m hold at each step.
- Baseline computed from last 48h during low-traffic window (03:00-06:00 PT).
- Canary fleet uses model variant v2.3-quant and fallback to v2.2 if model OOMs.
- This doc focuses on latency and smoke checks, not billing or infra capacity.

Quick TL;DR for oncall:
- Watch p95 and p99: if p95 > baseline+40ms OR p99 > baseline+150ms for 5 continuous minutes -> PAUSE rollout and notify SRE + Serving Runtime.
- Watch error rate: 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute increase -> PAUSE and triage.
- Watch KV-cache hit-rate drop > 10% relative -> investigate routing/kv warming.

Preflight checklist (to complete before starting rollout):
- [ ] Confirm canary autoscaler config mirrors prod (min pods, metrics hooks).
- [ ] Verify model binary deployed to canary nodes and checksum verified (sha256).
- [ ] Run cache-warm job (see linked_artifacts RL-1426) and verify hit rate > 85% on canary nodes for a synthetic warm set.
- [ ] Create a transient dashboard snapshot and share link in the launch thread.
- [ ] Confirm Slack rotation (channel #launch-latency-gatekeeper with 3 responders).
- [ ] Post canary plan and timeline to #release-ops 30m before start.

Latency gate thresholds (operational):
- baseline_p50 = query from last 48h
- baseline_p95 = query from last 48h
- baseline_p99 = query from last 48h
- hold thresholds: p50 > baseline_p50 + 40ms; p95 > baseline_p95 + 40ms; p99 > baseline_p99 + 150ms
- sustained condition window: 5 minutes
- soft-warning window: 1 minute (alerts for ops to watch)

Day-of calendar (timeline):
- T-60m: final preflight signoff by product and SRE (command: /ok-launch).
- T-30m: start posting incremental updates to #release-ops. Snapshot dashboards and synthetic smoke results.
- T-10m: run smoke-suite (see smoke checklist below) against canary endpoint.
- T: start traffic shift to 10% with gradual ramp over 2 minutes.
- T+10m: evaluate telemetry; if green, schedule shift to 30% at T+40m.
- T+40m: shift to 30% over 2 minutes, hold 30 minutes.
- T+80m: shift to 60% over 5 minutes, hold 30 minutes.
- T+120m: shift to 100% over 10 minutes.
- T+140m: post-launch smoke run and cross-team retrospective invite.

Smoke checklist (fast, low-noise tests):
- [ ] Basic generation smoke: 50 requests of 128 tokens, measure completion success rate and token latency.
- [ ] Chat session warmup: 20 short chat sessions that exercise context window and tool-calling path.
- [ ] KV cache diagnostics: run KV-hit probe (script id: kv_probe_v3) and log per-node hit rates.
- [ ] Rate-limit edge-case: 10x burst of small requests to validate throttles.
- [ ] Error monitoring: validate no increase in model OOM or 5xx for 15 minutes post-shift.
- [ ] Fallback verification: artificially throttle canary nodes and ensure fallback to v2.2 triggers and returns non-500s.

Rollback criteria (immediate):
- Any sustained p99 spike > baseline_p99 + 300ms for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows.
- 5xx rate increase > 1.0% absolute for 10 minutes.
- Customer-visible degradation: SLO alert from product metrics (latency-based) fires.
- Any sign of KV-corruption or cache invalidation affecting >10% of sessions.
- In case of rollback: notify #release-ops, post rollback reason and commit id, run postmortem template stub (link in linked_artifacts).

Monitoring and observability runbook snippets:
- Dashboards to watch: "Latency Gatekeeper - p50/p95/p99 by route", "KV hit rate by node", "Error rate by response class", "Autoscaler probe failures".
- Quick queries:
  - p95_query: service.latency.percentile(route, 95, last_5m)
  - kv_hit_query: service.kv.hit_rate(node, last_15m)
  - error_rate_query: sum(errors[5m]) / sum(requests[5m])
- Pager rules: use soft-alert to Slack (ops) at 1min threshold, page SRE at 5min.

Release notes draft (to be refined by product):
- Headline: "Improve tail latency for short-form generations (hosted API)"
- Summary: "This deploys batching and routing refinements that reduce median and p95 token latency for short prompt lengths. Customers using default routing should see faster small completions and more consistent interactive experiences."
- Changes: "routing policy tuned to favor warmed cache nodes; batching default window reduced from 25ms to 20ms for sub-512 sequences; model variant v2.3-quant introduced with conservative memory budget."
- Known issues: "In rare cases under cold start with long-context sessions (>8k tokens), users may observe slightly increased memory churn leading to transient 502s. Fallback to v2.2 is configured and should prevent widespread errors."
- Migration notes for customers: "No API changes. If you pin a model or use Dedicated, consult the Dedicated/Private rollout notes (product will send targeted comms)."

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we shorten hold windows to 15m for low-risk customers? Pros/cons item for next retro.
- Add a synthetic workload that more closely resembles enterprise prompt mixes (Riley to produce dataset).
- Verify that the autoscaler probe timeout of 10s is safe for new model variant (Tom to validate infra PR #6234).

After-action quick template (post-launch):
- Share dashboard snapshot and three bullet summary in #release-ops (time, outcome, rollback? yes/no).
- Fill lightweight incident doc if any halted step occurred.
- Schedule 30m retro the next business day if any threshold tripped.

Appendix (helpful pointers and scripts):
- smoke-suite command: scripts/smoke/run_smoke.sh --suite latency-gatekeeper --count 50
- kv probe script: scripts/ops/kv_probe_v3.py --nodes canary --output csv
- dashboard snapshot: create via observability UI -> Share -> Snapshot (attach link here in launch thread)

Notes to readers: this is still a working document. If you edit, please add initials and short note at the bottom with timestamp so we can track changes in Drive history.

Recent edits:
- 2027-04-09 (Aisha) added hold thresholds and calendar cadence.
- 2027-04-12 (Daniel) clarified rollback p99 tolerance and added kv_probe reference.

Unresolved: need product signoff for known issue language before external release notes go out.
